source.snippet: We operate a multi-region AI workflow orchestration platform running on Kubernetes across three AWS regions: us-east-1 eu-west-1 ap-southeast-1. Architecture overview: Kubernetes clusters in each region, Apache Kafka for workflow events, gRPC for service-to-service communication, Redis for transient workflow state, PostgreSQL with a single write primary and regional read replicas. Approximately 400 microservices handling workflow execution. Under normal load (~15,000 concurrent workflows), the system b...

problem_statement: Multi-region AI workflow orchestration platforms experience distributed state divergence under high concurrency when using Kafka + Redis + Postgres across regions, with pods appearing healthy but workflow execution producing inconsistent results.
target_segment: Platform/infrastructure engineers at mid-to-large companies running multi-region Kubernetes-based workflow orchestration at scale (10k+ concurrent workflows)
notes: Company context is clear — 400 microservices, 15k concurrent workflows, multi-region AWS. Real operational cost: state divergence in production AI workflows means incorrect automation outcomes. Buyer is an engineering team at a company with significant AWS spend. Single signal here, but the problem class (distributed state consistency in multi-region event-driven systems) recurs frequently in infrastructure communities. No explicit 'I'd pay' but the scale and professional context imply meaningful budget.
